hypothesis: When a paused request waits a long time before native readmission, changing its waiting position alone may be insufficient. Compare queue ordering with actual capacity funding of that same online-selected request.
proposed_controls: oldest already-output paused request first, queue movement only
same online queue order plus bounded funding of one complete native restoration

available_interfaces.queue: waiting.remove_request / prepend_request, with target override disabled for queue-only
available_interfaces.forced: existing staged_store_rotation begin prepare -> commit_reason recheck -> running.remove(victim) -> scheduler._preempt_request -> start_protection(target)
available_interfaces.admission: No force-admit API. Existing patched waiting loop targets request, native scheduler/connector performs actual allocation/load/admission; post-native receipts and first real output required.

differences.fit_first: Previous fit-first changed target to another currently free-fit waiter; this proposal funds the same oldest paused target.
differences.current_guard: Previous current guard chose a different victim only after a running allocation failed; it neither reordered nor funded waiting requests.
differences.capacity_victim: Existing capacity-victim prepare/commit is the nearest reusable action, but used tracker-proposed targets instead of a fixed oldest-paused comparison. This reuse does not establish novelty.

minimum_safety: Target still PREEMPTED/waiting with prior real outputs and no partial owned KV
Known full-history allocation requirement and current physical free blocks
At most one qualified running victim with sufficient uniquely owned blocks for the bounded first implementation
Recheck target/victim status, physical ownership, transfer completion, pending work and native in-flight reservations at commit
Native full saving backend retained; no selective-save clipping hidden in the new policy
No claim from a plan: verify actual preempt, native admission, new output and all affected-request costs
Short protection through first real output is part of the intervention cost, not attributed solely to victim eviction
unresolved_before_freeze: Pick one justified activation condition and service target without a parameter sweep
Confirm native full-save adaptation of old forced prepare/commit path does not change backend or transfer semantics
Explicitly freeze whether this is one-action mechanism pilot or repeated policy; no retrospective choice
rejected_shortcut: Truthful partial host match is structurally supported, but short load alone does not reduce full-history KV residency required before first new output and can be preempted again; do not launch that as a standalone optimization based on interface feasibility.
claim: Research design checkpoint, not a new algorithm or positive result.
